transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Jared (Orion Head of ML), Priya (Platform), Carlos (SRE)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros and then we want to understand your latency targets, concurrency, and what workloads you're thinking about.
[00:12] Jared: Yeah thanks. I'm Jared, we run the inference platform at Orion. Our main use case is customer support chat and financial assistant prompts. For chat we need p95 below about 250ms for short turns, and for longer doc summarization we're ok with higher. Also streaming is important, we stream tokens progressively.
[00:28] Priya: Hi, Priya here. Platform team. We care about bursts up to 350 concurrent users during market open, typical concurrency baseline is 60-80. Average prompt length is 120 tokens but tail can be ~1k tokens.
[00:40] Ethan: Great, thanks. Just to clarify, when you say p95 250ms, is that for full response latency or time-to-first-token streaming?
[00:48] Jared: Primarily time-to-first-token for the conversational short-turns. Full generation can be a few seconds but first token needs to be snappy.
[00:54] Carlos: And we need to ensure encryption at rest with KMS, SSO via SAML, and audit logs - so private could be interesting.
[01:05] Maya: Totally. High level, Hosted gets you fast onboarding and we run the models in our cloud. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and better isolation and consistent throughput. Private is the on-prem/VPC option with customer-managed networking and KMS integration.
[01:20] Ethan: On the perf side: the big levers are model size, quantization, batching, KV cache for chat, and the serving topology - dedicated instances let us pin GPU types and keep KV local to reduce p95.
[01:35] Jared: Can you give ballpark token/sec and p95 numbers? We want to compare to our in-house A100 setup.
[01:41] Ethan: Sure. Ballpark - on our hosted configs using g5-like acceleration for small chat models, time-to-first-token p95 for short 64-token completions is often ~120-220ms depending on region and network. For larger LLMs on dedicated A100 or H100 variants, steady-state token/sec for streaming is model-dependent: smaller 7B-ish models can do thousands of tokens/sec across a batch, but single-stream token/sec is lower. Important distinction: p95 often dominated by routing/network and cold-cache model loads.
[02:10] Priya: We're sensitive to network hops; our SRE team observed some variance with external endpoints. If we go hosted, what's the typical network RTT budget?
[02:18] Ethan: We usually see ~30-60ms for intra-region routing in major clouds, but your client environment and NAT/proxy adds variability. That's one reason customers prefer Dedicated in same VPC or Private with direct peering for sub-100ms RTTs.
[02:30] Jared: For concurrency - 350 concurrent streams - how does Redwood handle continuous streaming? Do you shard across GPUs or multiplex?
[02:38] Maya: Both. We have continuous batching and a routing layer. For Hosted we do multi-tenant packing with intelligent batching; Dedicated gives you reserved pools that reduce noisy neighbor issues. For very high sustained concurrency, dedicated or private gives more predictable p95s.
[02:50] Carlos: What about KV cache warmness? A chat-heavy workload benefits heavily from KV cache, right?
[02:55] Ethan: Exactly. If you have long multi-turn chats, local KV cache avoids re-encoding tokens; that significantly reduces end-to-end latency for subsequent tokens. With Dedicated we can keep KV on node-local memory longer. Hosted still caches but eviction policies are stricter across tenants.
[03:10] Jared: Ok, so next: we want to run token/sec benchmarks. We do a 1k-token prompt to simulate doc summarize. For streaming chat we want many short prompts. Can Redwood run those with controlled concurrency and return p50/p95/p99?
[03:22] Ethan: Yes, we can run both. We'll parameterize by model variant, sequence length, batch size, and concurrency. We'll produce time-to-first-token and tokens/sec metrics.
[03:30] Priya: Also need to know cold-start behavior - when a model hasn't been hot on node, what's the p95 penalty?
[03:36] Ethan: Cold-starts can add hundreds of ms to a few seconds depending on model and whether weights are preloaded. We have warm-pool strategies in Dedicated and Private to avoid that. For Hosted, we use active hot-pools for popular models but there's still a cold-tail. We'll include cold-starts in the benchmark.
[03:52] Jared: Any gotchas for comparing to our on-prem A100?
[03:55] Ethan: Hardware differences matter - A100 vs H100 vs g5 - and kernel/compilation layers. Quantization also changes throughput/latency and occasionally quality. We'll include quantized and FP16 runs. Also streaming APIs can affect perceived latency - chunk sizes, flush frequency matter.
[04:10] Carlos: Security checks - SOC2, SAML, KMS - you mentioned Private supports KMS. How is key management done?
[04:16] Maya: For Private, keys can be customer-managed in their KMS/HSM; Hosted supports envelope encryption and Redwood-managed KMS but can integrate customer KMS for dedicated contracts. We'll send SOC2 and network diagrams.
[04:28] Priya: For dedicated reserved capacity pricing, do you have examples for 3-6 month pilots?
[04:33] Maya: Yep, I'll send pricing tiers and sample commitments - also options for burst capacity for peaks.
[04:38] Jared: Can you walk through a sample p95 target calculation? Like, first token budget 250ms -> what should we expect with Dedicated in same VPC?
[04:46] Ethan: If you colocate in same VPC and pick a dedicated pool on H100-ish hardware, we can aim for sub-200ms time-to-first-token for small chat models. But you'll need KV warm, minimal network hops, and small prompt sizes. We'll include realistic numbers from our benchmark runs.
[05:00] Priya: About observability - what telemetry do we get? We need per-token latency breakdowns for routing, decode, network, and model compute.
[05:07] Maya: Redwood Console provides token-level breakdown, per-route dashboards, tracing hooks and retention options. We'll show examples in the technical deep dive.
[05:15] Jared: Perfect. For the benchmark, we'll give you sample prompts and concurrency patterns. Priya will export the logs.
[05:22] Priya: Will do. Expect to send by Monday.
[05:25] Ethan: Great - action items recap at the end.

[44:00] -- (wrap up, logistics) --
[44:12] Maya: Recap: Redwood to send benchmark template, SOC2 and network docs, pricing examples; Redwood SE to run token/sec/p95 runs (hosted vs dedicated), Orion to share prompt corpus and concurrency stats. We'll follow up to schedule a dedicated infra deep-dive week of 2025-12-29.
[44:30] Jared: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[44:34] Carlos: Thanks.
[44:36] Maya: Thanks all, bye.
